rows.notes: The document is explicitly a review paper/scoping report (CABI, STFC UK/Australia AgroClimate programme) synthesising literature, policy documents and a stakeholder workshop. It contains no primary experiment, field trial or validated model on spectral/thermal stress detection reducing pesticide use. Its only own activities are a literature search (web of science/CABDirect counts), a stakeholder workshop compiling opinions (Tables 3 and 6), and brief mention of two pilot studies from the same funding (an irrigation dataset from EO and a mechanistic mapping of Metarhizium acridum kill speed from ERA5 temperatures), none of which concern spectral/thermal detection or pesticide application. Where remote sensing detection is discussed (Poblete et al. 2020, Raza et al. 2020, Hornero et al. 2020, Zhang et al. 2016, Fuentes et al. 2021 etc.) the results are cited from other work and concern detection or damage mapping, not demonstrated reduction of prophylactic pesticide applications; the report itself notes that once damage is detectable, in-season intervention value is often limited. Hence no own evidence on the claimed effect; at most the cited detection studies support a precondition of the claim.
